dedupe_keys.name: fao methodology for damage and loss assessment in agriculture statistics working paper 19 17

description: This working paper sets out FAO's agriculture-specific methodology for assessing the damage and loss that disasters cause, meant to standardise impact assessment in a sector that general post-disaster assessments often underestimate. It defines key concepts, explains how the method differs from existing frameworks, and gives formulas and notation for computing damage to assets and loss of production in crops, livestock, forestry, aquaculture and fisheries, with optimal and minimal data requirements, strengths and weaknesses, a proposed information system from data to indicators, and its role in reporting for the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction and the Sustainable Development Goals. It was written by Piero Conforti, Mira Markova and Dimitar Tochkov and published by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in Rome in 2020 as Statistics Working Paper 19-17. It is generic and applicable to any country or region. The paper is a free PDF under the CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO licence. Caveats: it is a method, not a dataset or software, so results depend on national data on prices, yields and stocks, and non-commercial terms limit reuse. For simulation it provides standard damage and loss functions by agricultural subsector that exposure and resilience models can use to turn hazard impacts into economic losses. It is related to the FAO disasters in agriculture damage and loss record in this catalogue, which reports results of this method.
